what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/keep-copies-in-step: whether every copy of a person's things is in step, each device's report, and settling a record two copies changed apart, over the person's own rows.

payload.label: See if my copies are in step
payload.job: Show me whether every copy of my things is in step, and which records two of my devices changed apart
payload.description: Reads and changes nothing: the device rows, the records kept apart and the records they name come in with the request. Answers devices (each device's state, waiting changes and when it last caught up; a copy of your records you send in positions is shown once, as the device that named it or as a copy of its own) and versions (each record kept apart of the kind you name as thing_type: the record as it is now first, then one side per other version, with the words of its keep button). other_kinds names the kinds of other records kept apart, to ask about next.

thing_type.description: The kind of record whose versions to read or settle (one kind per call; other_kinds names the rest)

positions.description: How far each copy of your records took: [{ copy, settled_at }]

devices.description: Your device rows as they are kept (setting:catch_up_devices, its list), newest first: [{ device_id, title, kind, state, waiting, at, seen_at, copy? }]

records.description: The records kept apart and the records they name: [{ id, type, value }]; a record not sent is read as absent

payload.label: Say how this device stands
payload.job: Work out how this device of mine stands (caught up, offline or still holding changes) as the device list to keep
payload.description: Reads and keeps nothing. Takes one device's report: device_id (the id the device keeps for itself), state, waiting (the changes it still holds), at (when its writes last reached your store), title, kind and copy_id (the copy of your records it keeps), with your device rows as devices. Answers the report as the next device list (devices) for you to keep, and written: true; the list changes only when what you would see changed, or when the device's last catch-up moved by more than an hour; at most 40 devices are kept, newest first. When nothing changed it answers written: false and no list.

now.description: The time to report at (ISO); now when left out

devices.description: Your device rows as they are kept (setting:catch_up_devices, its list), newest first
The next device list to keep, when written is true

payload.label: Settle two versions
payload.job: Work out how to settle a record two of my devices changed apart: keep one version, keep both, or keep a merged one
payload.description: Reads and keeps nothing. Works out what you chose for one record kept apart (id, from see-if-my-copies-are-in-step): keep one (side, the id of the version to keep), both (each other version is kept as a record of its own, named after it with -kept- and a number that no record in records holds yet), or merged (value, the merged record). thing_type is the kind of the record; records are the kept-apart record and the records it names, as you read them. Answers writes: the chosen record first and the kept versions removed after it, for you to keep in one write, each standing on the record as it was handed in (expected, null for a record nobody had), so every copy takes it like any change.

id.description: The record kept apart, as the read names it

thing_type.description: The kind of record whose versions to read or settle (one kind per call; other_kinds names the rest)

records.description: The kept-apart record and the records it names: [{ id, type, value }]

writes.description: The records to write in one write: { id, type, value, expected }

payload.label: Answer the page that says how this device stands
payload.job: Answer the Trillion page route POST /work/api/catch-up/here: keep how this device stands and answer the page as old Trillion did
payload.description: A page route tool: the engine runs it for the page's account with { path, method, query, body, browser } and answers the page with { status, body }. POST /catch-up/here with { device_id, state, waiting?, at?, title?, kind?, copy_id? } keeps that device's row in setting:catch_up_devices (written only when what the person sees changed, or its last catch-up moved by more than an hour; newest 40 kept) and answers 200 { device, written }. A refused report answers 400 { error }; any other path or method answers 404 { error: "Not found" }. The write stands on the rows it read; rows another device changed meanwhile are read again.

stored.description: What this run reads of the person's own things, read by the caller from where the person keeps them (the engine keeps none) and given here: records: [{id, type, value}] of setting (the row setting:catch_up_devices), as this row's `stored` lists. What is not given is not there.

keep.description: What the run made, for the caller to keep where the person keeps it: rows {id, type, value} (value null removes), settings {label, value}, files {file, base64}. The run itself writes nothing.
